answer: Escalating registration work: each new agent identity must solve a proof-of-work puzzle bound to a unique hardware key, with difficulty doubling per identity from that key. The first costs seconds, the tenth costs hours, the hundredth costs weeks of compute. A sybil farmer's expense grows like a ripple widening outward — every fake more costly than the last — while an honest user with one identity pays almost nothing, a pigment-thin fee of a few seconds. Like a falcon that must hunt before it earns its perch, each identity must prove real work before it can vote or earn.
